paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The crowd chased Jesus across the sea, and He told them why: "it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill." (John 6:26) They wanted more bread. Jesus wanted to give them Himself. I think that's the question for every baker: am I here for the snack, or for the One who gave it?

When they asked what work God wants, Jesus made it simple: "The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent." (John 6:29) Then He said, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst." (John 6:35) Cookies on my counter go stale by Tuesday, and I've made peace with that. This Bread doesn't. Jesus says the manna fathers "ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died," but whoever eats this bread "will live forever." (John 6:49, 51)

And look at who holds the whole thing together. Jesus says, "No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him," and "the one who comes to Me I will never drive away." (John 6:44, 37) He also says it's the Father's will that He "shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day." (John 6:39) So if you're hungry for Him, baker, that's no accident, and you won't be turned away. Come to Him, believe in Him, and stay close, because He says whoever feeds on Him "remains in Me, and I in him." (John 6:56)
